best_for: Developers and small companies testing a distributed SQL database on a laptop before running it on Linux servers, who should check the license rules before going to production.

points.title: Free for small companies, with telemetry
points.text: The Enterprise Free license gives every feature at no cost to businesses with under USD 10 million in yearly revenue, counting parents and affiliates. It renews yearly, gets community support only, and the cluster must send telemetry. Government bodies do not qualify.

points.title: Clusters need a license key
points.text: A self-hosted cluster without a valid key is throttled to 5 open SQL transactions at once, 7 days after it starts. Single-node clusters and `cockroach demo` need no key and are never throttled.

points.title: Bigger companies pay or trial
points.text: Above the revenue limit you get a 30-day trial, also with telemetry, then need a paid Enterprise license. Paid licenses can turn telemetry off.

points.title: Windows is for trying it out
points.text: Cockroach Labs calls the Windows binary experimental and not fit for production. Use it to learn and test, and deploy on Linux or Kubernetes.

points.title: Plain archives, no installer
points.text: Each release is a zip on Windows (x64) and a tar archive on macOS and Linux, for x64 and Arm64. You unpack it and run the `cockroach` binary from a terminal.

points.title: Every platform keeps the full history
points.text: This site lists 257 versions for each of Windows, macOS and Linux, which helps when you need a binary that matches the version your cluster runs.
